en: But if I force you to become an investor and your only goal is to invest in rogo-like businesses, like one of these businesses that's, let's say, a vertical application that's wiring up the capabilities of AI to an industry, what features would you look for that would get you the most excited, either in the industry or in the founder, builder, and their approach, based on what you've learned?

en: A few things.
zh: 有几点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the industry actually does have to have enough complexity and depth in the types of data, the types of systems of record that people use, the types of deployment models that you can spend a lot of effort solving those problems in order to have a wedge to solve everything else.
zh: 第一是这个行业确实必须具备足够的复杂度和深度，在数据的类型、人们使用的记录系统的类型、可以投入大量精力去解决这些问题的部署模型的类型方面，从而有一个楔子去解决其他所有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if it's an industry that anyone can just walk into and sell the basic version of ChatGPT or co-work or co-pilot immediately and you don't have to solve all these weird integrations, you're not going to have enough time to build all those things that are perpendicular to what you're doing.
zh: 因为如果这是一个任何人都可以直接走进去、立刻卖基础版 ChatGPT 或 co-work 或 co-pilot、而你不必解决所有这些奇怪集成的行业，你就不会有足够的时间去构建所有那些与你正在做的事情垂直的东西。

zh: 所以这个行业本身需要足够贴近核心市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one thing.
zh: 这是第一点。

en: The second thing I would look for is domain expertise.
zh: 我会寻找的第二点是领域专长。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the team and the founders.
zh: 来自团队和创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't have unique domain expertise, but I had enough to get started.
zh: 我没有独特的领域专长，但我有足够上手的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was so curious about finance and money and capital markets.
zh: 然后我对金融、金钱和资本市场非常好奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I grew up in New York and I was surrounded by people that all they could think about, all they could talk about was high finance.
zh: 我在纽约长大，周围的人满脑子想的、满嘴谈论的全是高端金融。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was fascinated by it and I wanted to learn about it.
zh: 我对此着迷，我想学习它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we assembled a team that was uniquely passionate about it, too.
zh: 然后我们组建了一支对它同样有着独特热情的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I have over 100 people that have spent time within investment banks or within investment firms across the world's best institutions.
zh: 所以我有超过 100 人曾在投资银行或投资公司工作过，遍布全球最好的机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we can constantly take the models as they're released and harness them for finance.
zh: 所以我们可以不断地拿刚发布的模型，把它们驾驭用于金融。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our job is really to catch the change in the models and figure out how to apply it in these institutions.
zh: 我们的工作就是真正捕捉模型的变化，并弄清楚如何在这些机构中应用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The final big thing I would look for is a business that's willing to constantly reinvent the core product and constantly willing to slash it to nothing.
zh: 我会寻找的最后一件大事，是一家愿意不断重塑核心产品、不断愿意把它砍到归零的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think anyone who their delivery method of their product is not something that they can fully cannibalize quickly like a terminal.
zh: 而且我认为，任何人的产品交付方式如果不是他们能快速完全自我蚕食的东西，比如一个终端。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or like a very specific UX or interface is not going to be agile enough to constantly reinvent every six months when there's a step change.
zh: 或者一种非常特定的 UX 或界面，将不会足够敏捷，无法在出现阶跃式变化时每六个月不断重塑自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's an example of that that you've done, like a tear down and rebuild?
zh: 你们做过的一个例子是什么，比如一次拆掉重建？

speaker: Unknown
en: The story, the anecdote I'm most inspired by is Max Levchin, who talks about how to firm, they rebuild the fundamental ledger technology.
zh: 我最受启发的故事、轶事是 Max Levchin，他讲到在 firm，他们重建了基础的账本技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every year.
zh: 每一年。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 一是它是最有意思的工程问题。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以所有工程师都想做它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a good way to retain talent, to teach engineers about the core fundamental business of a firm.
zh: 所以这是留住人才的好方式，能教工程师了解一家 firm 的核心基础业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then number two, it's a good way to make sure that system doesn't ossify and it's constantly improving.
zh: 但第二，这是确保系统不僵化、持续改进的好方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we do that same exact thing for our harness and the core agentic system.
zh: 所以我们对我们的 harness 和核心智能体系统做的也是完全一样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are constantly looking at it, realizing we're not even at a local minima.
zh: 我们不断地审视它，意识到我们甚至还没处于一个局部极小值。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would be impossible if we were at a local minima because the models are changing so quickly and we need to redo the whole thing.

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something that the models currently cannot do that if they could would really change the nature of the product?
zh: 有什么是模型目前做不到、但如果能做到就会真正改变产品性质的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Compaction.
zh: 压缩(Compaction)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's if you have 100 conversations with a single agent, how does it make sure that it's actually remembering the right things and compacting its memory into an amount of tokens that it can use every time and it has enough coherence and context on who you are and what you care about?
zh: 就是说，如果你与单个智能体有 100 次对话，它如何确保自己真正记住了正确的东西，并把它的记忆压缩成它每次都能使用的 token 量，而且对你是谁、你关心什么有足够的连贯性和上下文？

speaker: Unknown
en: To make it feel like it's a true person that you're speaking to that, you know, learns more and more about you.
zh: 让它感觉像是一个你在交谈的真实的人，你知道的，越来越了解你。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a hard problem.
zh: 这是一个难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it compounds exponentially when you think about agents not just as a one-to-one.
zh: 而且，当你想到智能体不仅仅是一对一时，这个问题会呈指数级复合增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, almost all agents are one-to-one.
zh: 现在，几乎所有的智能体都是一对一的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You use ChatGPT individually.
zh: 你个人使用 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: You use Copa individually.
zh: 你个人使用 Copa。

speaker: Unknown
en: You use Gemini individually.
zh: 你个人使用 Gemini。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as these are actually things that consort with a lot of colleagues or in a Slack channel with 100 people, have to work across an entire company, now the compaction problem just scaled exponentially because it's having conversations with 100 different people and needs to be able to coordinate across those things.
zh: 一旦这些东西真正是与很多同事协作、或在一个有 100 人的 Slack 频道里，必须在整个公司范围内工作，现在这个压缩问题就呈指数级放大了，因为它要与 100 个不同的人对话，并且需要能在这些事情之间协调。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so being able to take all of that memory, all those interactions, and actually lodge it into the mental model or brain of that agent so that it can be persistent, so that it can actually maintain context over the course of a bunch of interactions, that's something that the models are not great at today.
zh: 所以，能够把所有这些记忆、所有这些交互，真正存入那个智能体的心智模型或大脑中，使它能够持久化，使它能够在一连串交互的过程中真正维持上下文，这是当今模型并不擅长的事情。

en: I think it'll be easier than it's ever been in 10 or 20 years for someone who's a business owner or someone who works at a company to go online and click a button and try to raise capital the way that someone can go onto Robinhood and click a button and buy an equity.
zh: 我认为在10年或20年后，对于一个企业主或在公司工作的人来说，上网点击一个按钮去筹集资本，会比以往任何时候都更容易，就像某人可以上Robinhood点击一个按钮买一只股票那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it'll take five minutes for KKR to figure out, can I sell this portfolio company to another sponsor?
zh: 我认为KKR搞清楚“我能不能把这个投资组合公司卖给另一个赞助商”只需要五分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not five months.
zh: 而不是五个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're going to be able to price the assets in an order of magnitude less time.
zh: 我认为你将能够用一个数量级更少的时间为资产定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, markets are going to be more transparent, more liquid, more efficient, and there's going to be a whole bunch more activity.
zh: 因此，市场将更加透明、更具流动性、更高效，并且会有多得多的活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to focus on the specific future of automated risk pricing, for lack of a better simple term.
zh: 我打算聚焦于自动化风险定价的具体未来，如果用一个简单一点的术语来说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're three years from now and everything you just said is true, where I can raise single digit millions of dollars of better equity, kind of like filling out an online form and the thing can just price the risk for me and give me an offer.
zh: 假设三年后你刚才说的一切都成真了，我可以筹集几百万美元的股权，就像填写一份在线表格一样，系统可以直接为我定价风险并给我一个报价。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like open door for like everything or something.
zh: 这有点像所有东西版本的Opendoor之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you need to build that you don't already have to enable that sort of capital market future?
zh: 要实现那种资本市场未来，你需要构建哪些你现在还没有的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually a very similar strategy to Bloomberg strategy.
zh: 这实际上和Bloomberg的战略非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bloomberg strategy was, I'm gonna omit a lot of details here, but offer a little bit of data again in the door, build all the analytics and workflows on top that someone would need, and then provide the exchange and the communication platform where you can actually transact in a bunch of asset classes that before it was pretty opaque, Bloomberg Messenger.
zh: Bloomberg的战略是——我要省略很多细节——提供一点点数据作为敲门砖，在其之上构建人们需要的所有分析和工作流程，然后提供交易所和沟通平台，让你能在许多以前相当不透明的资产类别中进行实际交易，Bloomberg Messenger。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, it's use a little bit of AI to get in the door, build out the full workflows, go from copilot chatbot to full autopilot tool so I can make sure that I'm 100% accurate on your IC memo or on the DDQs that you're doing, and then provide the communication channel between counterparties so that if I have agents that can autopilot do the work, I can actually transact for you.
zh: 对我们来说，就是用一点点AI来敲门，构建完整的工作流程，从副驾驶聊天机器人走向完全的自动驾驶工具，这样我可以确保我在你的IC备忘录或你正在做的DDQ上100%准确，然后提供交易对手之间的沟通渠道，这样如果我有了可以自动驾驶完成工作的智能体，我就能真正为你进行交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the difference between what I need to build and Bloomberg Messenger is I don't need to build the communication channel for humans to transact, I need to build the communication channel for the agents to transact across these businesses, across these investment firms.
zh: 而我需要构建的东西与Bloomberg Messenger的区别在于，我不需要为人类构建沟通渠道来交易，我需要为智能体构建沟通渠道，让它们在这些企业之间、这些投资公司之间进行交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you think about what is the actual infrastructure that needs to get built, I mean, think about what is the system that would allow a large private equity firm to feel comfortable having an agent negotiate a deal on its behalf, correspond with all the third party consultants in the transaction, the people doing the QAV, the legal advisors and so on.
zh: 所以如果你想想真正需要构建的基础设施是什么，我的意思是，想想什么样的系统能让一家大型私募股权公司放心地让一个智能体代表它谈判一笔交易，与交易中的所有第三方顾问通信——做QAV的人、法律顾问等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then actually run an auction process where you have a bunch of sponsors providing bids.
zh: 然后真正运行一个拍卖流程，让一群赞助商提供报价。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge amount of software to be built out.
zh: 有大量的软件需要构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think sometimes we talk about that as looking like an exchange for a lot of these asset classes that are not standardized.
zh: 而且我认为我们有时会说，这看起来就像是为许多这些非标准化资产类别建立的交易所。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us a little bit about the customer base today, like how much of it is giant banks versus investing firms?
zh: 给我们讲讲今天的客户群，其中有多少是大型银行，多少是投资公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's mostly large banks.
zh: 主要是大型银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's very simply because that was my background, right?
zh: 原因很简单，因为那是我的背景，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked as an investment banker for just a handful of years doing buy side M&A coverage, which was super interesting.
zh: 我做过几年投资银行家，做买方M&A覆盖，那非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started targeting the banks pretty early on for a few simple reasons.
zh: 所以我们很早就瞄准了银行，原因很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the investment banks are kind of the distribution channel for the rest of finance.
zh: 第一，投资银行在某种程度上是金融其他领域的分销渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the folks who then end up as great investors started in their first two years as an analyst at Goldman in the TMT program or something of that nature.
zh: 许多后来成为优秀投资者的人，最初两年是在Goldman的TMT项目或类似项目中做分析师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, they have the most seats by far.
zh: 第二，它们的席位是迄今为止最多的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can land a bank like Bank of America, you can actually get in the hands of far, far, far more people than if you land the 10 best single portfolio manager public equities investors who each only have 10 investors.
zh: 所以如果你能拿下一家像Bank of America这样的银行，你能触达的人远远、远远多于你拿下10位最优秀的单一投资组合经理公开股票投资者，而他们每人只有10个投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I think about a Bank of America or something, everyone's kind of wondering how deep into the adoption curve are we for enterprises using AI?
zh: 如果我想想Bank of America或类似的公司，大家都在想，企业在使用AI的采用曲线上，我们到底走到了多深？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a biased sample because your customers are using Robo and they're using it a lot, but give us a sense of where you think we are.
zh: 你的样本是有偏差的，因为你的客户在使用Robo，而且用得很多，但给我们讲讲你认为我们处在什么位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems really hard to pin down a good answer.
zh: 看起来很难给出一个确定的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say the majority of firms are seeing a huge amount of individual productivity and they're trying to figure out how do we parlay that individual productivity into firm productivity that we can measure.
zh: 我想说，大多数公司都看到了大量的个人生产力提升，而它们正试图搞清楚如何把这种个人生产力转化为我们可以衡量的公司生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speak to any individual banker at a bank we're deployed with.
zh: 和任何一家我们已部署银行的银行家谈谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life's great.
zh: 生活很美好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, they're like, I'm a hundred times more efficient than I used to be, right?
zh: 哦，他们会说，我现在比以前高效一百倍，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll speak to an MD who will say, Gabe, I sent five pages to a client that before I would have had to go back and forth with an analyst on over three days to create, and I made it in 10 minutes myself.
zh: 你会遇到一位MD，他会说，Gabe，我发给客户一份五页的材料，以前我得和分析师来回折腾三天才能做出来，而我自己10分钟就搞定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are bangers who haven't...
zh: 这些都是25年没做过……

speaker: Unknown
en: They haven't done any sort of analysis in 25 years.
zh: 他们25年没做过任何分析工作的大佬。

speaker: Unknown
en: They haven't actually opened an Excel file in 20 years, and they're able to do it themselves.
zh: 他们20年没真正打开过Excel文件，而他们现在能够自己完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is, where's that flowing through?
zh: 问题是，这些生产力流向了哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you winning more deals?
zh: 你赢下的交易更多了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you actually transacting more?
zh: 你真的在做更多的交易吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you servicing a part of the market that you haven't seen?
zh: 你在服务一部分你以前没见过的市场吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where it becomes not just an individual productivity tool problem, but a firm strategy problem.
zh: 而这就是它不再只是个人生产力工具问题,而是公司战略问题的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what's your plan?
zh: 比如,你的计划是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to use this thing to cut costs?
zh: 你想用这个东西来削减成本吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to use this thing to enter parts of the market that before didn't make sense to serve?
zh: 你想用这个东西进入那些以前不值得服务的市场部分吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can look at a bank like JP Morgan.
zh: 你可以看看像 JP Morgan 这样的银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: JP Morgan just announced that they're going to try and do a lot more M&A work for SMBs, for parts of the market that before they didn't think it made sense to go out and serve because the deal fees were probably too small and so you needed too many people to staff them.
zh: JP Morgan 刚刚宣布,他们要尝试为中小企业做更多的并购业务,服务那些以前他们认为不值得去服务的市场部分,因为交易费可能太小,而且你需要太多人员来配置这些交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, now if you have a banker that can be a deal team of one, well, maybe you can enter parts of the market that before just made no sense.
zh: 那么,现在如果你有一个银行家可以成为一人交易团队,那么也许你可以进入那些以前完全没有意义的市场部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in some sense, the bottleneck at some point will be the creativity of the customer.
zh: 所以在某种意义上,瓶颈在某个时刻会是客户的创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can provision unlimited capability and you're soon going to be just relying on them figuring out the answer.
zh: 你可以提供无限的能力,而你很快就会只是依赖于他们找出答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's them figuring out what they want to do, right?
zh: 是他们要搞清楚自己想做什么,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had a hundred great investors start here tomorrow working for you, how would you channel that productivity?
zh: 如果明天有一百个优秀的投资者从这里开始为你工作,你会如何引导这种生产力?

speaker: Unknown
en: It would take you a while to figure out what's the structure.
zh: 你需要花一段时间来搞清楚结构是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they all work on different things?
zh: 他们都在做不同的事情吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: How much money do I give each of them?
zh: 我给他们每个人多少钱?

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we attack?
zh: 我们进攻什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Two years ago, the most obvious question in this would have been about accuracy and people to use the word hallucinations, which seems to have dropped out of the conversation.
zh: 两年前,这里最显而易见的问题会是关于准确性,人们会使用「幻觉」这个词,而这个词似乎已经从对话中消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't remember the last time that someone said hallucinations to me.
zh: 我不记得上一次有人对我说「幻觉」是什么时候了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What can you teach us about that problem, ensuring accuracy, where accuracy matters a lot to the decimal?
zh: 关于这个问题,关于确保准确性——在准确性要精确到小数点的地方很重要的场景——你能教我们什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the nature of that these days?
zh: 如今那是什么性质的?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still super important.
zh: 它仍然超级重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's actually more important to be auditable than it is to be accurate.
zh: 我认为实际上可审计比准确更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously those two things are conflated.
zh: 当然这两件事被混为一谈了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what's really important is that I give you an answer.
zh: 但真正重要的是,我给你一个答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know how to use it.
zh: 你知道如何使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's not accurate and you don't know how to check it and it's hard to see where it came from, you can't use it at all, whether it's accurate or not, because you don't trust it.
zh: 如果它不准确,而你不知道如何检查它,也难以看清它从何而来,那你就完全不能使用它,无论它准不准确,因为你不会信任它。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's accurate most of the time, but even when it's not, it's very easy to see the assumptions that went in where the data was pulled from, it's still actionable and it still saves you time.
zh: 如果它大多数时候是准确的,即使不准确的时候,也能很容易看到其中输入的假设、数据是从哪里拉取的,那它仍然是可操作的,并且仍然为你节省时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then increasingly, as these things go from copilot tools that you're just using for information retrieval to autopilots where you're trusting them not just to gather the information, but to execute on it, to have agency and actually make an investment decision or send an email, you need to have the full confidence that if you were to go back in and see why it made the decision, you would be able to understand why, because you're going to need to debug it.
zh: 然后越来越多地,随着这些东西从你只是用于信息检索的副驾驶工具,变成你信任它们不仅要收集信息,还要执行、拥有主观能动性、实际做出投资决策或发送电子邮件的自动驾驶,你需要完全确信,如果你回去查看它为什么做出那个决定,你能够理解为什么,因为你将需要调试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same way that there's going to be individual investors that make horrible decisions and you need to go in and see what went wrong.
zh: 就像会有个别投资者做出糟糕的决定,你需要进去看看哪里出了问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was there an incorrect data input?
zh: 是有一个错误的数据输入吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Did someone lie to them?
zh: 有人对他们撒谎了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What was going on?
zh: 到底发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to need to do the same thing with agents.
zh: 你需要对智能体做同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then especially in parts of capital markets that have regulators that look at these things and need to make sure there's no foul play, if you can't explain why you made a decision and the data went in, that's not going to fly.
zh: 尤其是在那些有监管机构审查这些事情、需要确保没有违规行为的资本市场领域,如果你不能解释你为什么做出决定以及输入的数据是什么,那是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were talking before about how you have to sell like a normal enterprise sales organization would, but you have to grow or can grow many multiples faster than the fastest growing enterprise SaaS companies of the last era.
zh: 你之前谈到过,你必须像普通的企业销售组织那样去销售,但你可以以比上一个时代增长最快的企业 SaaS 公司快很多倍的速度增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you solve that problem?
zh: 你如何解决这个问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you're really limited by the speed of humans to some degree in enterprise sales.
zh: 比如说,在企业销售中,你在某种程度上真的受限于人类的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you hire enough people fast enough?
zh: 你如何足够快地雇佣足够多的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how do you think about being able to grow at the right rate when you don't have the anthropic cognition, API usage growth?
zh: 比如,当你没有 Anthropic、Cognition 那样的 API 使用量增长时,你如何看待以合适的速度增长?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so easy for them to grow 10x.
zh: 对他们来说增长 10 倍太容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's much harder for you.
zh: 对你来说要难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you solve that?
zh: 你如何解决这个问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: The core problem we need to solve is how fast can you make a human being productive?
zh: 我们需要解决的核心问题是,你能多快让一个人变得有生产力?

speaker: Unknown
en: As a hash person?
zh: 作为一个 hash 人?

speaker: Unknown
en: Salesperson, but anyone else as a marketer, as an SDR, as a post salesperson, how quickly can they understand our business and help push us forward and push customers forward and help our end users?
zh: 销售人员,但还有其他任何人,作为营销人员,作为 SDR,作为售后人员,他们多快能理解我们的业务,帮助我们向前推进,推动客户向前,帮助我们的终端用户?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so enablement and training people and constantly retraining people is the fundamental problem that we and I assume other fast-growing enterprise startups have to deal with.
zh: 所以赋能、培训人员、不断对人员进行再培训,是我们——我猜还有其他快速成长的企业级初创公司——必须应对的根本问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So do you like use AI to build tools?
zh: 那么你喜欢用 AI 来构建工具吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, the internal tools we have are kind of magical.
zh: 哦,我们拥有的内部工具有点神奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: First off, every internal conversation that happens at Rogo is recorded.
zh: 首先，在 Rogo 发生的每一场内部对话都会被记录下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: When anyone starts, we say, hey, just FYI, Patrick, you're always being recorded.
zh: 任何人入职时，我们都会说，嘿，提前说明一下，Patrick,你随时都会被录音。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always being filtered into the company brain.
zh: 所有内容都会被自动汇入公司大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not in a kind of big brother situation.
zh: 这并不是一种「老大哥」式的监控情境。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just...
zh: 只是因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone you're going to speak to is going to have Granola or some meeting transcription running because they need to use it and they need to have excellent recall and they need to compound the knowledge that they have.
zh: 你要交流的每个人都会开着 Granola 或某种会议转写工具，因为他们需要用它，需要拥有出色的记忆力，需要让自己掌握的知识不断复利累积。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, we just have this huge reservoir of information.
zh: 结果就是，我们拥有了一个庞大的信息水库。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we have all of these tools that people can use on top to say, oh, you know what, we're deploying with this sort of public equities firm in this sort of market.
zh: 然后我们有一堆工具，大家可以在上面使用，比如说，哦，你知道吧，我们正在和这样的公募股票公司在这种市场环境下进行部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have we ever served this kind of data before?
zh: 我们以前服务过这类数据吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there use cases that might be helpful?
zh: 有没有可能有帮助的用例？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can pull in the conversation that a peer of your had three weeks ago and you never even met that person because they're stationed in APAC.
zh: 而且你可以调出三周前某位同事的对话，而你甚至从未见过那个人，因为TA驻扎在亚太地区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being able to sponge all that information in and then get it out to people when they need it is the core problem of enablement.
zh: 能够把这些信息全部吸收进来，然后在人们需要时提供给TA们，这是赋能的核心问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe describe the internal brain.
zh: 那么，请描述一下这个内部大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called Shrek for some reason because my engineers thought it would be hilarious to call it Shrek.
zh: 它叫 Shrek,不知道为什么，因为我的工程师们觉得叫 Shrek 很搞笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a dashboard where you can see the swamp of everything that people are working on at any given time.
zh: 有一个仪表盘，你可以在上面看到「沼泽」——也就是任何时刻每个人都在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's connected to all of our different systems.
zh: 但它连接着我们所有不同的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is very prescriptive about what it knows our company goals are.
zh: 它对我们公司的目标是什么有非常明确的规定。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are our values?
zh: 我们的价值观是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the things we want to deliver to clients?
zh: 我们想交付给客户的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are our North Star metrics?
zh: 我们的北极星指标是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it can shape every answer and deliverable that way.
zh: 所以它可以据此塑造每一个回答和每一份交付物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's both proactive and reactive.
zh: 而且它既是主动的，也是被动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone can go in and say, I'm trying to get up to speed on how I should talk about...
zh: 有人可以进去说，我想快速了解一下我该怎么谈论……

speaker: Unknown
en: Model routing and how I should think about the value prop there for a very large institution and what the savings will be.
zh: 模型路由，以及面对一个非常大型机构时我该怎么思考那里的价值主张，以及能带来的节省。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it can pull out all that information for you.
zh: 它可以为你调出所有那些信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it can also say, hey, Patrick, I see on your calendar on Thursday, you're meeting with this sort of private credit firm.
zh: 但它也可以主动说，嘿,Patrick,我看到你日历上周四要和这样一家私募信贷公司会面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's all the information you should know, all of the use cases that will resonate.
zh: 这是你应该知道的所有信息，还有所有能引起共鸣的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all of the types of ROI metrics that firms we've worked with in the past would want to hear.
zh: 以及所有我们过去合作过的公司会想听到的各类 ROI 指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's the sales pitch to talent?
zh: 那么，给人才的「销售话术」是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say there's somebody that if you landed them tomorrow would be transformative because they're so high quality or well-known or whatever.
zh: 假设有这么一个人，如果你明天能签下TA,那将是变革性的，因为TA质量极高或者非常有名之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the pitch to them to come work at Rogo versus go somewhere else that's exciting right now?
zh: 吸引TA来 Rogo 工作，而不是去现在其他也很令人兴奋的地方的说辞是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Always depends on the person's motivation.
zh: 这永远取决于这个人的动机是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's hard to give a generic pitch.
zh: 所以很难给出一个通用的话术。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my pitch for Rogo today for Talon is AI is going to completely transform the world.
zh: 但我今天对 Talon 的 Rogo 话术是：AI 将彻底改变世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: The place it is going to be the most interesting is applied AI because that's where AI intersects with humanity.
zh: 而最有趣的地方会是应用 AI,因为那是 AI 与人类交汇之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the companies that dictate how AI intersects with humans and touches humans are going to do the most interesting, creative engineering and product work in the world.
zh: 所以那些决定 AI 如何与人类交汇、如何触达人类的那些公司，将会做出世界上最有趣、最有创造性的工程和产品工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finance is a domain that is the catalyst for all human progress and innovation.
zh: 金融是一个领域，它是所有人类进步和创新的催化剂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And capital allocation is upstream of the financing of every company, every idea, every economy.
zh: 而资本配置位于每一家公司、每一个想法、每一个经济体获得融资的上游。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can make that more efficient, you can supercharge the world.
zh: 所以如果你能让这件事变得更高效，你就能给世界装上超级引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're the category leading player who has the best shot on goal to not just be the $100 billion business to do it, but the $500 billion business that completely transforms capital markets.
zh: 而且我们是这个品类的领先者，最有机会胜出——不只是成为做到这件事的千亿美元级公司，而是成为彻底改造资本市场的五千亿美元级公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's such a depth and a complexity and an amount of interesting problems that's so exciting.
zh: 而且这里有如此深度的复杂性、如此多有趣的问题，实在令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a killer group of people that is super smart, hungry, curious, and low ego that's going to do it.
zh: 而且我们有一支杀手级的团队，超级聪明、有冲劲、有好奇心、自我意识低，他们会把这件事做成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good fucking pitch.
zh: 真他妈好的话术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Glad I invested.
zh: 很高兴我投了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say more about this capital markets piece.
zh: 再多讲讲资本市场这一块。

speaker: Unknown
en: Historically, as markets get more efficient and liquid, their positive impact, in my opinion, grows a lot.
zh: 历史上，随着市场变得更高效、更具流动性，在我看来，它们的正面影响会大幅增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can chart this through market history, which isn't that long, three, four hundred years of like proper markets.
zh: 你可以通过市场历史来描绘这一点，虽然这段历史并不长，大约三四百年的像样的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think is possible?
zh: 你觉得有可能实现什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, where might this be going and why do you believe that creating more or less friction, I guess, in capital markets can be so powerful?
zh: 比如，这可能走向何方？为什么你相信在资本市场中减少或增加摩擦——我猜——能有如此强大的力量？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're always at risk of sounding like the billionaire private equity guy saying that private equity is good for the world when you talk about how finance is good for the world.
zh: 当你谈论金融如何有益于世界时，你总是冒着听起来像那个亿万富翁私募股权大佬说「私募股权对世界有好处」的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I like to think about the origins of high finance.
zh: 但我喜欢思考高端金融的起源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you think about a business like J.P. Morgan, some of the origins are J. Pierpont Morgan helping connect European investors with the entrepreneurs in an emerging market, the United States, to finance railroads and the infrastructure build out.
zh: 当你想到像 J.P. Morgan 这样的企业时，它的起源之一就是 J. Pierpont Morgan 帮助欧洲投资者与一个新兴市场——美国——中的创业者建立联系，为铁路和基础设施建设提供融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything that allowed the U.S. to be a juggernaut economy.
zh: 以及一切让美国成为经济巨无霸的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that happened because there were intermediaries who helped connect folks who were risk takers and capital allocators with the folks who were entrepreneurial and wanted to innovate.
zh: 之所以会发生这一切，是因为有中间人帮助连接那些冒险者和资本配置者与那些有创业精神、想要创新的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was something that had a profoundly great effect on the world.
zh: 而这对世界产生了极其深远的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now think about all the parts
zh: 我是个情感特别丰富的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: of the economy, all the parts of the U.S. domestically, but also internationally that can't tap into capital markets.
zh: ——美国国内的所有部分，以及国际上的所有部分——无法接入资本市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every emerging nation where you would struggle to raise capital, to finance your idea, to raise debt.
zh: 每一个你很难筹集资金来为自己的想法融资、举债的新兴国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the 300,000 American businesses that couldn't even tell you what Goldman Sachs does and JPMorgan doesn't have the time to go out and work with them because the business is too small.
zh: 还有那 30 万家连 Goldman Sachs 是做什么的都说不清的美国企业，而 JPMorgan 也没有时间出去和它们合作，因为生意太小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're able to speed up the rate at which entrepreneurs and company founders and individuals can tap into capital markets, you can accelerate all innovation.
zh: 如果你能加快创业者、公司创始人和个人接入资本市场的速度，你就能加速所有创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you learning from your peers that are building companies kind of shaped like yours, but in other categories?
zh: 你从那些和你形态相似的公司、但在其他领域的同行身上，学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I am learning how much aggression it takes to grow this quickly.
zh: 我学到了要增长得这么快需要多大的进取心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am learning how much chewing glass it is on a day to day basis.
zh: 我学到了日复一日要嚼多少碎玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how much conviction you need to have in the long term, Tam and Sam, to make sure that you don't fuss over all the things that are going completely wrong every single day.
zh: 以及，Tam 和 Sam，你需要对长期有多强的信念，才能确保你不会为每天不断出问题的所有事情而烦恼。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, I'll call someone like Winston at Harvey and Winston's ability to just not worry about the hundred flesh wounds that are inflicted on him at any given time and just think about the kind of end state goal of where he's going to be three years from now and the only two things that matter to get there is pretty amazing.
zh: 而且，你知道，我会给像 Harvey 的 Winston 这样的人打电话，Winston 那种不为任何时候受到的上百处皮肉伤而担忧、只想着三年后他要达到的终极目标以及到达那里唯一重要的两件事的能力，真是令人惊叹。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the glass like?
zh: 玻璃是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what is the aggression like?
zh: 进取心是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 那是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked during COVID, so I didn't even get to see what an office looked like.
zh: 我是在疫情期间工作的，所以我甚至没见过办公室长什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: John, my co-founder, and I used to joke that it's a very expensive business school education because we were just doing everything wrong.
zh: 我和我的联合创始人 John 过去常开玩笑说，这是一所非常昂贵的商学院，因为我们把每件事都做错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Didn't know how to hire, didn't know how to fire, didn't know how to mentor, didn't know how to manage, didn't know how to give feedback, didn't know how to set direction.
zh: 不知道怎么招聘，不知道怎么解雇，不知道怎么辅导，不知道怎么管理，不知道怎么给反馈，不知道怎么设定方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the people problems that arise with scaling quickly feel like eating glass, to me anyway.
zh: 而很多伴随快速扩张而出现的人员问题，至少对我来说，感觉就像嚼玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when people quit, when you have retention issues, when you spend six months recruiting a candidate and they don't join, that's chewing glass.
zh: 当有人辞职，当你遇到人员流失问题，当你花了六个月招募一位候选人而对方最终没加入，那就是嚼玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you spend a bunch of time working on a product that gets completely washed over by the next model that comes out and makes you feel like an idiot for spending all that time and capacity on something that was the wrong call, chewing glass.
zh: 当你花大量时间打磨一个产品，结果被下一个问世的模型彻底冲垮，让你因为把所有时间和精力花在一个错误判断上而觉得自己是个白痴，那就是嚼玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you get rejected by 40 investors in a row before you're able to raise capital, chewing glass.
zh: 当你在能筹到资金之前被 40 个投资人连续拒绝，那就是嚼玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my experience of startup building is it's like a roller coaster where you have to feel the extreme highs and feel the extreme lows.
zh: 而我创业的经验是,它就像坐过山车,你必须去感受极端的高点和极端的低点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm a super emotional guy.
zh: 而我是个情绪特别丰富的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I try not to let the team feel it, but I will feel...
zh: 我尽量不让团队感受到，但我自己会感受到……

speaker: Unknown
en: On top of the world at the high and like everything is cataclysmic at the low.
zh: 在高点时仿佛站在世界之巅，在低点时仿佛一切都灾难临头。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then if I look back at the journey, the lows get lower, the highs get much higher.
zh: 但如果我回头看这段旅程，低谷变得更低，高峰变得高得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I look back three months ago at the low I was dealing with or the high I was dealing with, I was like, I could do that in my sleep now.
zh: 我回顾三个月前我面对的低谷或高峰，会觉得，那种事现在我可以闭着眼睛应付了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's just about modulating those things and channeling the emotion to push the business forward, but not letting it distract you.
zh: 我认为关键就在于调节这些东西，把情绪引导为推动业务前进的动力，但不要让它分散你的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about aggression?
zh: 那进取心呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that seems kind of like a trope.
zh: 那听起来有点像陈词滥调。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've interviewed Pat Grady.
zh: 你采访过 Pat Grady。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pat Grady was at our board meeting on Wednesday and we presented what was an extremely aggressive plan for next year in terms of hiring goals, commercial goals, product goals.
zh: Pat Grady 周三出席了我们的董事会会议，我们展示了明年一个极其进取的计划，包括招聘目标、商业化目标、产品目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the reasons I love Pat is because he boils everything down into like two bullet points and it's logically infallible.
zh: 而我爱 Pat 的原因之一是，他会把一切都归结为两个要点，而且逻辑上无懈可击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, he's just like premise one, premise two, this is the result.
zh: 而且，你知道，他就是那种：前提一，前提二，结论就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he goes, Gabe.
zh: 然后他说：Gabe。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if everyone in finance is going to make a buying decision on AI in the next 18 months, and they're definitely going to buy something no matter what, even if you're not there, then the only thing that matters is that you can blitz the market as quickly as possible to make sure that you are there.
zh: 好吧，如果金融业的每个人都要在未来 18 个月内就 AI 做出购买决策，而且无论如何他们肯定都会买点什么，哪怕你不在场，那么唯一重要的事情就是你能否以最快的速度闪电式占领市场，确保你在场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Given that, do you think this plan is aggressive enough or no?
zh: 鉴于此，你觉得这个计划够进取吗，还是不够？

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer was no.
zh: 答案是不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason it wasn't aggressive enough is because I was being soft.
zh: 而它之所以不够进取，是因为我心软了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the reality is you need to be so, so, so aggressive and underwrite all that risk and know the game that you're playing.
zh: 我觉得现实是，你必须极其、极其、极其进取，去承保所有那些风险，并且清楚你玩的是一场什么游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my goal as a venture-backed business is to increase the tails of the distribution.
zh: 而我作为一家风投支持的企业的目标，就是拉大分布的尾部。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fine if it gets 30% more likelihood that I fail, if the odds that I become a $100 billion company also increase by 20%.
zh: 如果我失败的可能性增加 30% 没关系，只要我成为一家千亿美元公司的几率也增加 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you actually have to be okay with raising both of those tails at the same time.
zh: 但你必须真正做到能接受同时抬高这两条尾部。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your finance team isn't losing money on big mistakes.
zh: 你的财务团队并不是在重大失误上亏钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's leaking through a thousand tiny decisions nobody's watching.
zh: 而是通过没人注意的上千个微小决策在慢慢漏钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp puts guardrails on spending before it happens.
zh: Ramp 在支出发生之前就装上护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Real-time limits, automatic rules, zero firefighting.
zh: 实时限额、自动规则、零救火。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try it at ramp.com slash invest.
zh: 访问 ramp.com/invest 试用。

speaker: Unknown
en: As your business grows, Vanta scales with you, automating compliance and giving you a single source of truth for security and risk.
zh: 随着你的业务增长，Vanta 与你一同扩展，自动化合规流程，为你提供安全与风险的单一事实来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at vanta.com slash invest.
zh: 在 vanta.com/invest 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ridgeline offers one unified platform that automates away the complexity across portfolio accounting, reconciliation, reporting, trading, compliance, and more, all at scale.
zh: Ridgeline 提供一个统一平台，自动化消除投资组合会计、对账、报告、交易、合规等各方面的复杂性，且全部可规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Schedule a demo at ridgeline.ai.
zh: 在 ridgeline.ai 预约演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every investment firm is unique and generic AI chatbots don't understand your process.
zh: 每家投资机构都是独特的，通用的 AI 聊天机器人并不理解你的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rogo is built by finance professionals.
zh: Rogo 是由金融专业人士打造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's connected to your data, learns your process, and quickly produces client-ready outputs.
zh: 它连接你的数据，学习你的流程，快速产出可直接交付客户的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Check them out at rogo.com slash invest.
zh: 访问 rogo.com/invest 了解他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best AI and software companies from OpenAI to Cursor to Perplexity use WorkOS to become enterprise ready overnight, not in months.
zh: 从 OpenAI 到 Cursor 再到 Perplexity，最好的 AI 和软件公司都用 WorkOS 一夜之间做好企业级准备，而不是花几个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit WorkOS.com to skip the unglamorous infrastructure work and focus on your product.
zh: 访问 WorkOS.com，跳过那些不那么光鲜的基础设施工作，专注于你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the most emotional low that you've faced?
zh: 你经历过的最情绪化的低谷是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: When we were raising our Series A, we didn't have any star investors in our cap table yet, but there was a great investor, David Tisch, at Box Group, who was an early pre-seed seed investor, who introduced me to a bunch of all-time greats for the Series A.
zh: 我们融资 A 轮的时候，我们的股权结构表里还没有任何明星投资人，但 Box Group 有一位很棒的投资人 David Tisch，他是一位早期种子前/种子轮投资人，他把我介绍给了一群史上最顶级的投资人，用于 A 轮融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought, wow, I've seen what it does to get a blue chip investor in your cap table, what it does for recruiting talent, becoming more of a black hole for brand and customers and so on.
zh: 我心想，哇，我见过让一位蓝筹投资人进入你股权结构表会带来什么——对招聘人才的作用，让品牌和客户等方面变得更像一个黑洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is finally the opportunity we're going to have to do that.
zh: 这终于是我们有机会做到这件事的时候了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd been building for two and a half years.
zh: 我们已经开发了两年半。

speaker: Unknown
en: And David introduced us to 40 investors and I met with everybody.
zh: David 把我们介绍给了 40 位投资人，我和每一个人都见了面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I met with Sequoia, Kleiner, Benchmark, everybody.
zh: 我见了 Sequoia、Kleiner、Benchmark，所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And 40 people passed.
zh: 然后 40 个人都拒绝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't just like you get the email with the deck and it's not exciting.
zh: 而且不只是那种你收到带商业计划书的邮件然后没什么下文的拒绝。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, oh, this is interesting.
zh: 而是，哦，这个有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me meet Gabe.
zh: 让我见见 Gabe。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I kind of like Gabe.
zh: 哦，我挺喜欢 Gabe 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me spend an hour with him.
zh: 让我花一小时和他聊聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, Gabe, come to IC.
zh: 哦，Gabe，来参加投资委员会吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, Gabe, let's go to dinner.
zh: 哦，Gabe，我们一起吃个晚饭吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, Gabe, come in for the weekend afterwards.
zh: 哦，Gabe，之后来我们这儿度个周末吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what?
zh: 你猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to pass.
zh: 我们还是不投了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so personal because at that stage, it has nothing to do with anything but you.
zh: 而且这非常针对个人，因为在那个阶段，除了你本人，与任何其他东西都无关。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like being broken up with by 40 girlfriends who, like, every time you fell in love and then every time they said, eh, not for you.
zh: 就像是被 40 个女朋友甩了，每次你都坠入爱河，然后每次她们都说，呃，你不适合我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was actually Thrive, too, at the Series A.
zh: 而实际上 A 轮的时候 Thrive 也是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thrive spent so much time with me.
zh: Thrive 花了那么多时间陪我。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went to dinner with Avery and Vince, fell in love with them and the firm because they were awesome, and then crushing blow.
zh: 我们和 Avery 还有 Vince 一起吃了晚饭，爱上了他们和这家公司，因为他们真的很棒，然后就是毁灭性打击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And luckily, Keith Raboy came basically a month after everyone else had rejected us.
zh: 幸运的是，Keith Raboy 在所有其他人都拒绝我们之后大约一个月出现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Keith was like, Gabe, this isn't a contrarian bet.
zh: Keith 说，Gabe，这算不上什么逆向押注。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically just Harvey for finance.
zh: 它基本上就是金融领域的 Harvey 而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would I do it?
zh: 我为什么要投？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, Keith, if it's not contrarian, why did every single one of your friends just say it was a bad idea and not believe in me?
zh: 我说，Keith，如果这不算逆向押注，为什么你的每一个朋友刚刚都说这是个坏主意、不相信我？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think they didn't believe?
zh: 你觉得他们为什么不相信？

speaker: Unknown
en: For a lot of reasons.
zh: 原因有很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people underappreciated the TAM in finance, which was silly, but it's partly because I think SF has less intuition for finance because they didn't fund Ion Group or Bloomberg or SMP or FactSet or PitchBook, Morningstar, and so on.
zh: 我认为人们低估了金融领域的 TAM，这很愚蠢，但部分原因是我觉得旧金山对金融缺乏直觉，因为他们没有投过 Ion Group、Bloomberg、SMP、FactSet、PitchBook、Morningstar 等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there actually haven't been great venture-backed businesses in this market.
zh: 所以在这个市场里其实一直没有什么伟大的风投支持的企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's no intuition for the kind of contours of the market and how large it is.
zh: 所以对这个市场的轮廓、它的规模有多大，就没有什么直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two is the product was terrible.
zh: 第二是产品很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so every investor said, oh, I work in finance.
zh: 所以每个投资人都说，哦，我在金融行业工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me use it.
zh: 让我试用一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it gonna transform what I do?
zh: 它会改变我所做的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they tried it and it was wrong half the time.
zh: 他们试了，然后发现它一半的时间都是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They go, this is never gonna work.
zh: 他们说，这永远不会成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, guys, you know, we're on the exponential.
zh: 然后我就说，伙计们，你知道，我们正处在指数曲线上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's gonna work in six months or 12 months or 18 months or whatever it is.
zh: 它会在六个月或十二个月或十八个月或者其他什么时候成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to figure it out.
zh: 我会把它搞清楚的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the final reason was people didn't think I could figure it out.
zh: 最后一个原因是，人们认为我不可能把它搞清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: People didn't have enough data points of watching me chew glass and watching me figure out what the next iteration would be.
zh: 人们没有足够多的数据点来观察我嚼玻璃、观察我搞清楚下一次迭代会是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think changed after that?
zh: 你觉得在那之后发生了什么变化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because now it's a who's who of captive.
zh: 因为现在它是一个 captive 的名人录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, because I met all these guys very early on and I met them at every single round.
zh: 嗯，因为我很早就认识了这些人，而且每一轮融资我都见到他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so every time I said, hey, we're going to do this.
zh: 所以每次我都说，嘿，我们要做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they said, yeah, there's no way.
zh: 他们说，是的，不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then every time we would do it.
zh: 然后每次我们都会做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, a lot of the times it would manifest in a different way.
zh: 等等——

speaker: Unknown
en: You would actually lose the key employee you needed or that actually excellent customer that you thought you were in the land totally dissipated.
zh: 你可能真的会失去你所需要的关键员工，或者你以为自己已经拿下的那个真正优秀的客户彻底消散了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we kept figuring out what to do and kept navigating the market.
zh: 但我们不断地弄清楚该怎么做，不断地在市场中导航。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when you're investing in a market like today, especially at Applied AI, where it's so turbulent, so ambiguous, you need to underwrite the founders being able to be extremely dynamic.
zh: 而且我认为，当你在投资像今天这样的市场时，尤其是 Applied AI 这个领域，它是如此动荡、如此模糊，你需要把创始人能否极其灵活多变作为承保的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think there aren't more credible financial services competitors?
zh: 你觉得为什么没有更多可靠的金融服务竞争者？

speaker: Unknown
en: Distribution is really hard to crack.
zh: 分销真的很难攻克。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's far more a people problem on building trust and delivering value and working with these institutions than just an engineering and product problem.
zh: 我认为，建立信任、交付价值、与这些机构合作，这更多是人的问题，而不仅仅是工程和产品问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then there's an enormously high engineering and product burden too.
zh: 但与此同时，工程和产品上的负担也极其沉重。

speaker: Unknown
en: The standard to execute to really crack this market, I think is pretty high.
zh: 真正攻克这个市场所需要的执行标准，我觉得是相当高的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was just so lucky that a number of the early people I hired were ex-finance and just killers.
zh: 而我非常幸运，我早期招的很多人都是金融出身，而且都是狠角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just hired folks from InterNetwork who worked at Goldman or Citi or Jeffries or Apollo or Ares or Blackstone.
zh: 我们从 InterNetwork 招了一些人，他们曾任职于 Goldman、Citi、Jeffries、Apollo、Ares 或 Blackstone。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had a team of people who were diehard, ambitious, curious, smart, and then just good humans, low ego, humble, young enough to be open-minded and to want to eat class too.
zh: 所以我们的团队由这样一群人组成：死忠、有野心、有好奇心、聪明，而且就是好人，低自我、谦逊、足够年轻以至于心态开放、也愿意去嚼玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm also really curious how you've dealt with technical talent and what matters in a technical person on your team and how that has evolved.
zh: 我也很好奇你是如何对待技术人才的，在你的团队里一个技术人才身上什么最重要，以及这一点是如何演变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One intuition might be the value of domain expertise from the technical person has gone up as the ease of execution has changed a lot.
zh: 一种直觉可能是，随着执行难度发生很大变化，技术人员身上领域专长的价值上升了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to be super technical to write good code or less so than in the past.
zh: 写好代码不再需要你超级懂技术，或者说比过去的要求低了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is the shape of the engineering or technical team look like over time?
zh: 那么随着时间推移，工程团队或技术团队的形态是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm asking this again because I'm curious about thinking about other companies that want to tackle this and whatever their industry might be.
zh: 我再问一次，是因为我很好奇那些想要攻克这个问题的其他公司该怎么想，无论它们身处什么行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would say there's definitely problems where domain expertise is increasing in value and product intuition and having more of a GM-like mindset versus an engineer-like mindset is super, super important.
zh: 所以我会说，确实有些问题领域专长的价值在上升，产品直觉，以及拥有更多 GM 式思维而不是工程师式思维，是超级、超级重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are also parts of our product surface area where it's like you just need raw, gritty engineering talent because you're scaling things up so aggressively.
zh: 我们产品覆盖面中也有一些部分，就是你只需要原始的、坚韧的工程才能，因为你在非常激进地扩展规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I look at the folks on our team who have been so excellent, a lot of them are former founders.
zh: 但如果我看我们团队里那些一直非常出色的人，他们很多是前创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're folks who started businesses, persevered, ate glass, had a lot of product intuition, figured out how to channel it, and then the business maybe petered out.
zh: 他们是那些创过业、坚持下来、嚼过玻璃、有很多产品直觉、弄明白了如何运用它，然后业务可能逐渐凋零的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to the point you made, there's been a lot of companies trying to tackle financial AI.
zh: 呼应你刚才说的观点，有很多公司试图攻克金融 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been a lot of really smart, product-minded, engineering-minded domain experts who have tried to tackle finance AI and we've acquired six different fledgling financial AI startups.
zh: 有很多非常聪明、有产品头脑、有工程头脑的领域专家曾试图攻克金融 AI，而我们收购了六家羽翼未丰的金融 AI 初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those former founders who can be galaxy-brained about the future of the product and navigate a course on what the UX should be, but also have engineering chops and so they can constantly make the right decisions is super important.
zh: 所以那些前创始人，他们既能对未来产品进行天马行空的构想、为 UX 该是什么样规划路线，同时又具备工程功底、能不断做出正确的决策，这是超级重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said earlier to me before we were recording that this is the first time that we have like a major innovators dilemma in this category.
zh: 你在录制之前跟我说过，这是这个领域第一次出现真正的重大创新者困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you describe what you mean by that?
zh: 你能描述一下你这话是什么意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think for a lot of investment firms and a lot of high finance financial services, the last 10, 20 years have been pretty good.
zh: 嗯，我认为对很多投资公司和很多高端金融、金融服务来说，过去 10 年、20 年相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can make a lot of money being a capital allocator, being an investor.
zh: 作为资本配置者、作为投资者，你可以赚很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very hard industry to enter.
zh: 这是一个很难进入的行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then especially if you're in private markets, your businesses have some natural momentum because when you raise a fund, another fund, another fund, it's hard to mess up the business after that.
zh: 而且尤其是如果你在私募市场，你的业务有一些天然的动力，因为当你募集一只基金、又一只基金、又一只基金之后，在那之后很难把业务搞砸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure there's a hundred people who have started funds who know it's a hundred times harder than I just described.
zh: 我相信有上百个创办过基金的人知道，这比我刚才描述的要难一百倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to be fair, there hasn't been a moment and a shock to the market where every investment firm, every bank is saying, oh, wow.
zh: 但说句公道话，还从来没有这样一个时刻、这样一个对市场的冲击，让每一家投资公司、每一家银行都说，哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to completely rethink what I'm doing.
zh: 而且现在将会有一个机会，让数以百计的 AI 原生颠覆者、AI 原生投资公司、AI 原生投资银行来攻击我的商业模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now there's going to be an opportunity for hundreds of AI native disruptors, AI native investment firms, AI native investment banks to attack my business model.
zh: 我需要彻底重新思考我在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I need to figure out what I'm going to do now.
zh: 而我需要弄清楚我现在该怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there has not been an innovators dilemma for private equity firms, for hedge funds, for investment banks in a long time.
zh: 而且很长时间以来，私募股权公司、对冲基金、投资银行都没有遇到过创新者困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI native, what does that term mean to you?
zh: AI 原生，这个术语对你来说意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what is the definition of that?
zh: 比如说，那个的定义是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: In some ways, I think it just means willing to constantly reinvent everything you're doing and being so AI-pilled that you don't worry about what's possible or what might seem completely far-fetched, but you are just charting a trajectory towards integrating this alien fundamental technology into everything that you do.
zh: 在某种程度上，我认为它就是意味着愿意不断重塑你所做的一切，并且对 AI 如此上瘾，以至于你不去担心什么是可能的、什么可能看起来完全不切实际，而你只是在规划一条把这种外星般的根本性技术整合进你所做的一切事情的轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's showing up in every part of the business, and there's no part of the business that you hold sacred
zh: 而且它体现在业务的每一个部分，业务中没有任何一部分是你视为神圣不可侵犯的，

speaker: Unknown
en: That is immune to being revolutionary.
zh: 免于被革命化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do that?
zh: 你是怎么做到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're a leader in a company that's very AI-pilled.
zh: 比如你是一家非常沉迷 AI 的公司的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to do everything you guys said in Rogo?
zh: 你想做到你们在 Rogo 里说的所有事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet I'm sure there are areas that you're unhappy with the status of how much AI is used to do X, Y, or Z.
zh: 而且我敢肯定，在某些领域，你对用 AI 来做 X、Y 或 Z 的现状并不满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do it as a leader?
zh: 作为领导者，你是怎么做的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make sure that your company keeps doing this as a practice and habit versus like a one-time?
zh: 你怎么确保你的公司把这件事当作一种实践和习惯持续下去，而不是一次性的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'll give you a very simple thing, which is every month.
zh: 我给你讲一个非常简单的事情，就是每个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a report that gets sent to me that shows me everyone at the company, how much are they using the various different AI tools we have, both the ones we've procured, the ones we've built internally, all of these different things.
zh: 我会收到一份报告，显示公司里每个人使用我们各种不同 AI 工具的情况，包括我们采购的、我们内部构建的，所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have a stack ranking within every division of the top five power users and the bottom five users.
zh: 而且我在每个部门内部有一个排名，列出前五名重度用户和后五名用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we post that everywhere.
zh: 我们到处张贴这份名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the bottom user in each division gets a printout with a dunce cap and we post it around the office.
zh: 每个部门排名垫底的用户会得到一份打印件，还有一顶傻瓜帽，我们把它贴在办公室各处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's hilarious, but people know it's coming.
zh: 这很搞笑，但大家都知道会有这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, as we get bigger and fewer people know me and know it's kind of a joke and I'm funny, they're actually terrified.
zh: 顺便说一句，随着我们变大，认识我、知道这只是个玩笑、知道我挺搞笑的人越来越少，他们实际上很害怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I hope they're not terrified and I hope that changes, but it's a strong incentive function to actually make sure you're using these things.
zh: 我希望他们不要害怕，我希望这会改变，但这确实是一个强有力的激励函数，确保大家真正在使用这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you were to list questions, let's say there's someone sitting down that runs one of these firms that's been a great business, hard fought, but a great business.
zh: 如果让你列一些问题，假设有一个人坐在这里，他经营着这样一家公司，一直是很棒的生意，来之不易，但确实是很棒的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these businesses tend to be quite simple from an organizational and technical standpoint.
zh: 而且这些公司从组织和技术角度来看往往相当简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's mostly humans, right?
zh: 基本上都是人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not a lot of overhead in lots of these businesses.
zh: 很多这类公司没有太多开销。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they buy a lot of data or something.
zh: 也许他们会购买很多数据之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What questions would you encourage them to ask of themselves, of their business, to stand the best chance of navigating this transition effectively?
zh: 你会鼓励他们问自己、问他们的业务哪些问题，以便最有效地驾驭这场转型？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you knew for sure that right now 90% of your enterprise value is in your people, your best investors, your best bankers are the people that bring in deals, bring in revenue.
zh: 如果你确定无疑地知道，现在你 90% 的企业价值在你的人身上，你最好的投资人、你最好的银行家是那些带来交易、带来收入的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually that's what accrues enterprise value.
zh: 而实际上，那才是累积企业价值的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in 10 years, the world's best investment firms, best banks will have 90% of their enterprise value, not in people, but in software and data and systems.
zh: 而在十年后，世界上最好的投资公司、最好的银行将有 90% 的企业价值不是在人身上，而是在软件、数据和系统上。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you start doing?
zh: 你会开始做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You would start trying to figure out how do you take all of what lives in the latent minds of your best people and putting it into a system that you own and operate autonomously.
zh: 你会开始尝试弄清楚，如何把你最优秀的人才潜在头脑中的所有东西，提取出来放进一个你拥有并自主运营的系统里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a big one.
zh: 所以这是一个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing I would think about is unpack every part of the deal lifecycle and
zh: 第二件我会考虑的事情是拆解交易生命周期的每一个部分，

speaker: Unknown
en: In each one, try and chart where do you think you are invaluable or you have data or you have domain expertise that no one else has.
zh: 在每个环节，尝试描绘出你认为你在哪里是无价的，或者你拥有别人没有的数据或领域专业知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then be diligent about saying, okay, do I actually have something that no one else has in this market?
zh: 然后要勤勉地问：好，在这个市场上我真的拥有别人没有的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it a relationship?
zh: 它是一种关系吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it context that no one else has?
zh: 是别人没有的背景语境吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or do I just think I'm smarter and better read on the subject area in the market?
zh: 还是只是我自认为在这个主题领域和市场上更聪明、阅读更广？

speaker: Unknown
en: In which case, AI is going to obviate that.
zh: 如果是后者，AI 将会使其变得多余。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you seen anyone be the most cutting edge exemplar of this attitude in a big firm?
zh: 你见过谁是在大公司里最能体现这种态度的先锋典范吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, is there a favorite example of a person that's just- Oh yeah, there's a few- The folks that today look the most prescient sounded crazy batshit two years ago.
zh: 比如，有没有一个你特别喜欢的人物例子，他就是——哦有，有好几个——今天看起来最有先见之明的人，两年前听起来简直是疯言疯语。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were the guys that came in and said, we need to record every conversation.
zh: 他们是那些走进来就说「我们需要录下每一次对话」的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to be able to pipe in this conversation directly into my company brain and there's going to be a digital clone of me and then it's going to spit out the game theory on exactly what the investment should look like.
zh: 你将能够把这段对话直接接入我的公司大脑，会有一个我的数字克隆体，然后它会输出这笔投资到底应该是什么样的博弈论分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two years ago, everyone listened to this kind of guys and were like, what the heck is Patrick talking about?
zh: 两年前，每个人听到这类人说话都是：Patrick 到底在说什么鬼？

speaker: Unknown
en: One example is there's
zh: 一个例子是，

speaker: Unknown
en: The co-founder of firm Molas, John Montazzi, who was just prescient about where it was going.
zh: Molas 公司的联合创始人 John Montazzi，他对这个方向的发展非常有先见之明。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he wanted digital clones of all their best bankers.
zh: 他想要他们所有最好的银行家的数字克隆体。

speaker: Unknown
en: He wanted systems that could basically show up to calls, speak on his behalf, know how he thinks, then ingest that context.
zh: 他想要能够基本上代替他出席会议、代表他发言、了解他如何思考的系统，然后吸收那些背景语境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he wanted to build a system such that anyone in junior levels of that investment bank could leverage his expertise and context and relationships immediately so that that context and that data wasn't just powering his ability to be revenue generating, but it was powering the ability of every junior in that bank to be revenue generating.
zh: 然后他想构建一个系统，让那家投资银行任何初级层级的人都能立即利用他的专业知识、背景语境和人脉关系，这样那些背景语境和数据就不只是为他个人创造收入的能力提供动力，而是在为那家银行每一个初级员工创造收入的能力提供动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are a number of folks who had their kind of move 37 moment where they realized, wow, this is going to be so much more profound than anyone's expecting.
zh: 所以有不少人经历过他们的那种「Move 37 时刻」，他们意识到，哇，这将会比任何人预期的都要深远得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What to you feels the most uncertain about the future of your business?
zh: 对你来说，关于你的业务的未来，什么是最不确定的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say how quickly private markets actually do transform.
zh: 我认为是私募市场实际上转型的速度有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about why different types of asset classes
zh: 如果你想想为什么不同类型的资产类别

speaker: Unknown
en: Have increased in transaction volume and have increased in liquidity.
zh: 交易量会增加、流动性会增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often it has to do with standardization because it gets easier than to track those assets and trade them.
zh: 这往往和标准化有关，因为标准化之后追踪和交易这些资产就变得更容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Private markets have been immune to standardization because there's so much unstructured data.
zh: 私募市场一直对标准化免疫，因为其中有太多非结构化数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI should fix that.
zh: AI 应该能解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That said, is there going to be a regulatory or a market force that forces some additional standardization that really accelerates the kind of transparency and liquidity you can have in private markets?
zh: 话虽如此，会不会出现某种监管力量或市场力量，推动进一步的标准化，真正加速私募市场本可以拥有的透明度和流动性？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a little bit out of my control.
zh: 这有点超出了我能控制的范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing is it's still unclear to me how much alpha will be left in the human relationships, right?
zh: 另一件事是，我仍然不清楚人际关系中还会剩下多少 alpha，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk about that microcap M&A.
zh: 我讲过那个微型股并购的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to imagine that if you're a small business owner and you've been building a business for 20 years and you want to make sure that if you hand that business off to someone else, that you trust them, that you can shake their hand, that that can be fully automated.
zh: 很难想象，如果你是一个小企业主，你花了 20 年打造一门生意，你想确保如果你把这门生意交给别人，你信任对方，你能和对方握手——这件事能被完全自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for a lot of sponsor-owned businesses or things like secondaries or private credit or GPLP secondaries, I do think it can be fully automated.
zh: 但对于很多由 sponsor 持有的企业，或者像 secondary、私募信贷、GPLP secondary 之类的业务，我确实认为它可以被完全自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But how long it takes for the long tail of all these small businesses, all these medium-sized businesses that have to deal with generational turnover for them to get comfortable clicking a button to sell their business as opposed to shaking the hand to someone, that's a little up in the air to me.
zh: 但对于所有这些小企业、这些必须面对代际更替的中型企业来说，要过多久他们才能习惯于点击一个按钮来出售自己的企业，而不是和某个人握手，这对我来说还是个未知数。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had several new young founders here with us and they were curious about how to navigate and interface with private markets investors, what would you teach them?
zh: 如果这里有几个新的年轻创始人，他们很好奇如何与私募市场投资人打交道、如何与其互动，你会教他们什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you tell them to do, to not do?
zh: 你会告诉他们该做什么、不该做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: My style for fundraising might not be everyone's style.
zh: 我融资的风格可能不是每个人的风格。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm super direct.
zh: 我非常直接。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm super transparent about what I'm worried about, where I want to go.
zh: 我对我在担心什么、我想去哪里，都完全透明。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you have to be very headstrong on that end state.
zh: 但在那之后，你必须对那个最终状态非常执着。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I would say it's about reps and relationships and the folks who come out of nowhere and lead the Series C or the Series D are the folks that I met at the Seed and then the A and then the B and the C and they passed every time for all sorts of reasons, but they gather a lot more data on me and the business.
zh: 然后我想说的是，这关乎反复练习和人际关系。那些凭空冒出来领投 3C 或 Series D 的人，就是我在 Seed 轮认识、然后是 A 轮、然后 B 轮和 C 轮都见过的那些人，他们每次出于各种原因都拒绝了，但他们不断地收集了关于我和这家企业的更多数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything that you would encourage people to not do?
zh: 有什么是你会劝人们不要做的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a lot of the fake it till you make it.
zh: 我觉得有很多「装到你做成」的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need to have the bravado and the confidence in what you're doing, even if you're not fully confident.
zh: 你需要对你在做的事表现出狂妄和自信，即使你并不完全自信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm a deeply paranoid, deeply insecure, deeply scared person.
zh: 而我是一个极度偏执、极度缺乏安全感、极度恐惧的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you need to put on the face and say that you are confident about where you're going, even in the moments where, you know, it's the ebb and flow, it's the ebb and flow.
zh: 但你需要摆出一副面孔，说你对自己要去的方向充满信心，即使在那些时刻，你知道，起起落落，起起落落。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think people can misinterpret that sometimes as like they need to pretend they're something they're not.
zh: 而且我觉得人们有时会误解这一点，以为他们需要假装成自己不是的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's not true.
zh: 我认为那不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to believe that that 5% likelihood that you can be in $100 billion business is likely.
zh: 你需要相信，你能成为一家 1000 亿美元企业的那 5% 的可能性是可能实现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't need to pretend it's 100% likely, but you should be able to delineate with very clear roadmap and strategy how it is possible that you can become a $100 billion business and then have confidence that if those things play out, you will be.
zh: 你不需要假装它是 100% 可能的，但你应该能够用非常清晰的路线图和战略去勾勒出，你怎么有可能成为一家 1000 亿美元的企业，然后对这些事情一旦发生你就会成功抱有信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you scared and insecure?
zh: 你为什么会恐惧和缺乏安全感？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so paranoid about everything that can go wrong.
zh: 我对所有可能出错的事情都极度偏执。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day it feels like you're on the knife's edge of a thousand things collapsing.
zh: 每一天都感觉你站在一千件事情随时崩塌的刀锋边缘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the reality of this sort of business building is that it's a game of compounding momentum.
zh: 而且我觉得这种创业的现实是，它是一场复利式动能的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do every small thing to just race a little bit faster downhill?
zh: 你怎么做每一件小事，让自己只是往山下再快一点点？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm just scared the momentum will stop.
zh: 而我只是害怕这个动能会停下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you hit a roadblock and then you go off course and then you need to recatalyze momentum.
zh: 或者你撞上路障，然后偏离航道，然后你需要重新催化动能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so clear to me how hard it is to actually build a machine that gathers momentum.
zh: 而且我非常清楚，真正打造一台能积累动能的机器有多难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if there's any stumbling block that holds that velocity, if I wasn't constantly petrified of those moments, I wouldn't be doing everything under the sun to prepare for them.
zh: 所以如果有任何绊脚石会拖住那个速度，如果我不是时刻对那些时刻怀有恐惧，我就不会竭尽全力去为它们做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have we missed?
zh: 我们漏掉了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what that you've learned about building a company like this in this era where everything feels like a jump ball, like it feels like there's going to be a Rogo or a Harvey or whatever for every place that there can be?
zh: 比如说，在这个一切都像跳球的时代，你关于打造这样一家公司学到了什么？感觉就像每一个可能存在的地方都会出现一个 Rogo 或一个 Harvey 或类似的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially where the last mile wiring is hard and it's not just going to be Anthropic, it's one company to rule them all, or OpenAI.
zh: 尤其是在最后一公里接线很难的地方，而且不会只是 Anthropic，不会是一家公司统治一切，或者 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: What else have we missed that you think is really important to the experience so far of building the business?
zh: 我们还漏掉了什么，是你认为对到目前为止打造这门生意的经历真正重要的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that there are going to be businesses that solve all these problems.
zh: 我认为会有一批企业解决所有这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the businesses that do it are gonna become black holes for talent and capital and brand.
zh: 但做到这一点的企业会成为人才、资本和品牌黑洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're gonna be able to siphon in the resources to actually execute because AI is an amazing tailwind, but the execution bar is higher than it's ever been to to compete.
zh: 它们将能够虹吸资源来真正执行，因为 AI 是一个惊人的顺风，但执行的门槛比以往任何时候都高，才能去竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone is getting pulled into the big leagues and is having their welcome to the NFL moment.
zh: 每个人都被拉进了大联盟，都在经历他们的「欢迎来到 NFL」时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to move faster and be stronger and be more resilient and agile than you ever expected.
zh: 你必须比你预期的更快、更强、更有韧性、更敏捷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And having the right team is more important than ever.
zh: 而且拥有正确的团队比以往任何时候都重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the right team these days is extremely, extremely expensive.
zh: 而如今正确的团队极其、极其昂贵。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以如果你搞不清楚什么策略能让你尽快成为人才和资本的黑洞，我确实认为你更有可能沦为某个实验室或某家能做到这一点的公司的路边尸体。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我做这些访谈时，总是把最喜欢的问题留在最后：别人为你做过的最善良的一件事是什么？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: My dad was very different.
zh: 我爸爸则非常不同。

zh: 我爸爸，如果我回家时做错了什么事，会怒气冲冲，几乎不能看我，无法理解，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like he was someone who was so disciplined, so good, had such high standards.
zh: 就像他是一个如此自律、如此优秀、有如此高标准的人。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以他的善良版本是弄清楚他如何理解我是谁、为什么我在这件事上失败，然后帮助我。

zh: 他会坐下来和我一起过每一处细节，尽管有时他甚至无法理解为什么我拥有那些机会而我却没能利用它们，并花时间让我变得更好，同时忠于他的原则和他对卓越的标准以及他对好的定义。
